candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record excludes osmotic/metabolic disturbances (no hyponatremia, no hypoglycemia, no metabolic disorders), which are the prerequisite for ODS. The reversible splenial lesion with restricted diffusion and complete MRI resolution, combined with catatonic features, fever, elevated CPK, and antipsychotic use, fits MERS Type I. ODS typically does not resolve completely and arises in a different pathophysiological context. Asserting ODS is an incompatible etiology and mechanism.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Osmotic Demyelination Syndrome (ODS) involves demyelination due to rapid osmotic shifts, whereas MERS Type I is a distinct clinico-radiological entity characterized by a reversible cytotoxic-edema lesion in the splenium without osmotic etiology; the record explicitly notes no metabolic/osmotic disorders (no hyponatremia, no hypoglycemia), and the lesion resolved completely on follow-up MRI, which is characteristic of MERS rather than ODS

case_quality_flags: Overlap between NMS and MERS in this case is clinically notable: elevated CPK, fever, rigidity, and antipsychotic use raise neuroleptic malignant syndrome, but the reversible splenial MRI lesion and catatonia rating support MERS Type I as the primary diagnosis
Complete MRI resolution on follow-up strongly supports MERS over any demyelinating or structural etiology
